suggestions.suggestion: Optional follow-up coverage: assert that a second successful refetch cannot clear an existing dirty conflict, exercise rejected/throwing grant reads and failed mutation results while drafts are pending, and explicitly deny a JSONB null placement request on an archived course (distinct from SQL NULL). Existing source handles these paths conservatively; these are coverage opportunities, not observed logic defects.

release_gates.gate: Use a separately authorized real disposable local Supabase Auth/PostgREST stack with the merged migration and frontend. Verify named RPC dispatch and argument names, JSON error handling, relationship/nested SELECT shapes, persisted writes and exact readbacks. PGlite SQL and mocked Supabase component transport are not HTTP/service integration evidence. Parent-owned full merged DB/UI/lint/type/build/signed-out-HTTP checks must also finish green; this bounded review does not claim to have rerun those complete suites.

Exercise platform, granted staff, same-org ungranted owner/admin, revoked creator and no-grant identities through real authenticated requests and direct settings/access/catalog/entries/print/leaderboard/history URLs. Verify revocation without logout and fresh denied mutations. A signed-out redirect or JSDOM permission-state test does not satisfy this gate.

Verify actual local Storage uploads and registration, other-event/revoked/malformed-path denial, wrong-event/wrong-kind selection denial, scoped listing, denied overwrite/upsert/move/update/delete (including platform clients), and retained objects after failed registration/selection. Validate actual MIME/size service behavior and public delivery separately. Known public event-media URLs can remain downloadable after revoke/archive; no revocable-delivery claim is made. SQL metadata fixtures are not Storage HTTP/object-byte evidence.

Exercise real independent sessions in both orderings for submission versus event/contest archive, review/correction versus archive, and subsequent requests after committed revocation; include direct manager roster DML and Storage upload versus archive. Also exercise competing administrator grant writes. The frontend only reconciles reads it receives, cannot cancel an issued RPC or discover unfetched changes, and supplies neither compare-and-swap nor atomic lost-update prevention. Source locks and sequential PGlite tests do not prove concurrent scheduling.

Verify real Next RSC refresh and pending access/conflict interaction in a browser, mobile layout, keyboard/focus, popup image loading/errors/dismissal and five-second once-per-visit behavior across polling/token navigation, current shared logos, draft print readiness/pagination and all required elements. Decode/scan QR targets against the unchanged legacy-compatible /c/<token> route; exercise remembered golfers, retry UUIDs, CTP inches and unmeasured drive claims against the real local backend. JSDOM does not prove browser layout, print or QR scannability.

Before separately authorized publication, verify trusted Troy/platform-admin identity inventory, actual deployed policies/privileges including additional Storage policies, approved historical access assignments, catalog conflicts/incompleteness, backup/restore readiness and migration/application ordering. No blanket staff grants, inferred creators, fabricated complete distances or demo-seed reruns. Obtain human approval before any push, hosted migration or deployment. This local verdict closes neither rollout gates nor Kanban tasks.

reviewed_commits.assessment: Clean rows follow every successful new snapshot; dirty rows preserve selections and explicitly block when fetched authority changes, even when the draft now matches it. Conflict is sticky until Use latest access. Old rows stay mounted but disabled while current-event reads are pending or failed, and successful reads clear the error. Stable event/account keys preserve the actual MutationForm pending state. Checked mutation errors do not mark the draft clean; success clears dirty only when no conflict has been discovered. Neither refetch completion nor mutation completion silently resolves a conflict. RPC names/arguments and backend/route guards were not changed by this fix.
